name: Sarcoma of Cervix Uteri

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Cervical Sarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant spindle cells or other sarcomatous histology on cervical biopsy
Positive immunohistochemical staining for mesenchymal markers (e.g., vimentin, desmin, SMA) and negative for epithelial markers
MRI or CT showing a cervical mass with invasive characteristics without typical epithelial tumor features
Exclusion of cervical carcinoma by cytology and histology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of sarcomatous tissue with supportive immunohistochemical profile and exclusion of carcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires expert pathological review due to rarity and histological overlap with other cervical malignancies.

searchTerms: unusual white or yellow vaginal fluid

occasional.symptomName: Leg edema due to lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: swelling in legs from lymph blockage
leg swelling due to lymph fluid buildup
fatigue related to low red blood cells

rare.symptomName: Fistula formation between cervix and bladder or rectum
searchTerms: abnormal connection between cervix and bladder
leak between cervix and bladder or bowel

rare.symptomName: Lower extremity neuropathy due to nerve invasion
searchTerms: leg nerve pain from tumor invasion
lower limb neuropathy due to nerve involvement

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic blood loss
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous cervical mass with invasive borders
CT scan demonstrating local extension and possible lymphadenopathy
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; occasional detection of complex karyotypic abnormalities
other: Histopathology demonstrating spindle cell or pleomorphic sarcoma
Immunohistochemistry positive for vimentin, desmin, SMA; negative for cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of glandular epithelial malignant cells
More common in younger women with HPV association
Biphasic tumor with both carcinomatous and sarcomatous components
Immunohistochemistry positive for both epithelial and mesenchymal markers

redFlags: Persistent irregular vaginal bleeding unresponsive to treatment
Pelvic pain with neurological symptoms such as leg weakness or numbness
